intro: STL to USDZ converts STL models to USDZ on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to show a part in augmented reality on an iPhone before printing it, or send it to a client to see it at real size. USDZ is Apple's augmented reality format: on an iPhone or iPad it opens from Safari, Messages or Files and the model appears on the table at its real size.

STL is the format every slicer reads: it only stores triangles, with no units or colours. USDZ uses the Y axis up, so the STL model, with Z up as in 3D printing, is turned so it stands upright; the advanced options let you keep the axes. Choose the units of the STL and the USDZ.

The USDZ comes out as a single file with the mesh, its units in metres per unit and each face's colours, ready for Apple's Quick Look. You can apply a scale and keep the STL parts separate, merge them or get one per file in a ZIP.

The STL geometry is not simplified or repaired on its way to USDZ. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, and up to ten files per task. Each file is converted in an isolated process on our server in the European Union and deleted when it expires.
steps: Upload one or more STL files.
Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does the USDZ come out lying down?
faq.a: Because STL and USDZ do not use the same vertical axis. Tick or untick “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options.
Yes when the USDZ supports them (VRML, X3D and USDZ); STL stores no colours and the note says so.

faq.q: What if the STL has textures?
faq.a: STL textures are not converted: the geometry and each face's or material's colour go through.
